chunks: It is not worthy of the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the idolaters, even though they may be their relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are destined for Hell.
ai.seo_question: Why should the Prophet not seek forgiveness for his relatives if they are polytheists?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Ishtighfar) is often contrasted with the general permissibility of intercession for believers, highlighting that the prohibition here is specific to those whose fate is sealed in Hellfire after clear evidence. It underscores the distinction between divine decree and human supplication, noting that while the Prophet and Imams intercede for the faithful, they do not seek forgiveness for persistent polytheists, even kin like Khadijah or Hamza in some interpretations, once their disbelief is established.
